transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), John Keating (Avalon CTO), Sarah Li (Avalon Cloud Architect), Devon Park (Avalon PM), Nina Gomez (Avalon Security)

Auto-summary (auto): Kickoff to align on adaptor certification for the Redwood marketplace. Main blockers: KMS integration, VPC peering model, packaging expectations. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics: Marketplace packaging, helm/onprem installer, VPC/KMS, quantization compatibility, telemetry & logging, benchmark plan, timeline for listing.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, I run the partner integrations for marketplace. Quick roll call?
[00:10] John: John here, CTO at Avalon. Sarah, Devon, Nina are with me.
[00:15] Sarah: Hey, Sarah.
[00:17] Maya: Great. Rafael and Priya are our SEs, they'll drive the checklist and lab work. Goal for today is to unblock packaging and get a short plan for a certification lab.
[00:30] Devon: Yeah, we want to list in the marketplace and also publish a joint refarch doc. Curious about the packaging expectations and what counts as "certified".
[00:40] Rafael: Good question. Certification for us is mostly operational: deployability via helm or operator, KMS key-wrapping support for customer keys, clear telemetry points, and a basic performance baseline. There's also the security attestation check.
[00:53] Nina: On the security side we'll need the exact questionnaire. We have SOC2 Type II and an ISO cert but the listing needs specific answers about encryption-in-transit, at-rest, KMS, and audit logs.
[01:05] Priya: We'll share the questionnaire. One gotcha we often see is how teams handle K-V cache persistence and whether any keys are stored locally. We need a clear model from Avalon: where's the KV cache kept in your adaptor?
[01:20] Sarah: The KV store is ephemeral in our adaptor, we keep it in memory and if you enable persistent mode it'll use an optional Redis backed store. We planned to support Redis or our managed cache which can be its own service.
[01:35] Rafael: Okay ephemeral is fine for hosted; for dedicated/private customers we need the option to point at customer-managed Redis or use prefixing so cache keys don't collide. Also, Redis TLS + auth needs to be documented.
[01:48] John: We can add TLS and auth. For KMS, we support a few providers via a plugin: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and a PKCS#11 path for HSM. The PKCS path is what our regulated customers use.
[02:03] Maya: That's good — Redwood requires KMS or HSM compatibility for private deployments. We'll need to validate key wrapping and that private keys never leave HSM. Nina, will that be covered in your docs?
[02:15] Nina: Yep, I'll include specifics and a summary of HSM operations. Also will include our scan results.
[02:22] Devon: On packaging - do you expect a helm chart only or an installer bundle for on-prem?
[02:28] Priya: Helm chart plus a tarball for air-gapped installs is typical. The helm chart should expose values for imageOverride, resource limits, nodeSelector, and all the KMS/Redis endpoints. We also like a sample values.yaml for common configs.
[02:43] Sarah: We have a helm chart already, but it's minimal. We'll need to extend it to expose those values and add probes/readiness checks.
[02:50] Rafael: Probes are important. Also include liveness/readiness and a /metrics endpoint for Prometheus. For tracing we prefer OpenTelemetry instrumentation or an adapter that speaks OTLP.
[03:05] John: We can add OTLP and metrics. For metrics we currently expose basic counters and histograms but need to add per-route latency.
[03:14] Maya: Perfect. For the marketplace listing itself, a few non-negotiables: single-signon options (SAML/SSO) for enterprise customers, support statement for private deployments, and a short published SLA target for Dedicated. The listing metadata needs those fields filled.
[03:30] Devon: SLA for dedicated — sounds like you'd want us to commit to <100 ms p95? That might be aggressive given model variability.
[03:38] Rafael: It's per-profile. We baseline against a 512-token and 2048-token profile. For dedicated GPU pools we commonly see <80-120 ms p95 on small models, larger models are different. The listing can show expected ranges and Redwood adds a throughput label based on verified benchmarks.
[03:56] Priya: We'll run a quick benchmark in lab. Rafael will share the harness.
[04:02] Maya: On timeline — typical fast-track certs are 2-3 weeks if artifacts are ready. If security docs or the helm chart need work it can slip to 4-6 weeks.
[04:12] Sarah: We can try to hit the 2-3 week path. We'll need Redwood's checklist so we don't miss anything.
[04:18] Maya: I'll send a checklist today. It includes packaging, security questionnaire, sample values, telemetry expectations, and the benchmark script.
[04:26] Nina: A quick note about data residency: some of our customers require tokens never leave the EU. Does Redwood support region locking for hosted connectors?
[04:36] Rafael: Yes, route policy can pin requests to region and we have private deployments for fully air-gapped setups. For marketplace listing we indicate which regions we support.
[04:45] John: Another integration question — what about function calling / structured output? Our adaptor tries to map model outputs to structured events for downstream workflows. Any required schema?
[04:56] Priya: No enforced schema, but we prefer if you provide an example schema and samples in the refarch doc. We'll validate that function calling doesn't break stream semantics. Also ensure you respect stop tokens and streaming chunk semantics.
[05:10] Devon: For canary deploys — if we push a new adaptor version what rollback story does Redwood expect?
[05:18] Rafael: We typically require health checks, versioned images, and a canary route that sends a percentage of traffic to the new version. If error rate or latency regressions cross thresholds there's an automatic rollback. We'll document canary thresholds.
[05:33] Maya: Ok that maps well to Redwood's rollout feature. For the reference architecture doc — Priya will draft a public doc emphasizing supported deployment modes and an example network layout for VPC peering.
[05:45] Priya: I'll include a diagram showing hosted vs dedicated vs private, with plumbed-in KMS and Redis options.
[05:51] Sarah: Quick question: any specific RBAC requirements for the helm chart?
[05:56] Rafael: Minimal clusterrole/role permissions; ideally a namespaced install. For listing certification we prefer non-cluster-admin installs unless necessary. Document the permissions required.
[06:07] Nina: We'll sanity-check that for our air-gapped installs.
[06:10] Maya: Great. Any blockers from Avalon?
[06:14] John: Main blockers are finalizing the helm chart and the KMS PKCS#11 docs. We'll prioritize those.
[06:21] Maya: Okay, let's confirm owners in action items. We'll also schedule the lab run — Rafael and Priya will coordinate with Sarah for cluster access.
[06:30] Devon: Sounds good.
[06:33] Maya: Alright, wrap up: I'll send the checklist, sample values, and the benchmark harness. Avalon will share dev kubeconfig + security artifacts. We'll meet again after the lab run — proposal: 2026-02-03 for a 30-minute sync. Anyone opposed?
[06:49] John: Works for us.
[06:51] Nina: fine.
[06:52] Priya: Great. Thanks all.
[06:55] Maya: Thanks, closing out.

--- End transcript ---
notes: Meeting felt productive; Avalon is fairly mature on security and KMS which should speed certification. Helm chart needs modest additions; bench harness will expose latency characteristics. Consider offering a short co-branded refarch writeup as value-add.
